restaurant_name: โรงพยาบาลสัตว์เพ็ทฟูชา (PET FUUSHA PET HOSPITAL)
text:
Although I've used this animal hospital's services frequently, my recent experience has been very upsetting. Earlier this month, I brought my "son" (a male cat) here for neutering. Since I had business out of town that day, I left him at the hospital for three nights. I picked him up when I returned.

A few days later, my son started feeling unwell. He was panting, gasping for breath, and trying to meow but couldn't. I brought him back for a follow-up examination. The vet said it was likely because a blood test wasn't done before the neutering procedure, and that some cats aren't suitable for direct gas anesthesia, which could cause this adverse effect. The cat had a high fever that day, so the vet gave him a fever-reducing injection and performed an X-ray, which showed no problems with his heart or lungs. Then, they gave us four different medications without considering whether we could successfully administer them (and we were unsuccessful).

The story doesn't end there. Even worse symptoms followed. Three days after the first cat showed symptoms, the second and third cats started exhibiting similar signs. A few days later, all 11 cats in my household began showing the same symptoms: difficulty breathing (gasping for breath), high fever, and difficulty meowing. That's when we realized that the first cat was the problem. It wasn't a side effect of the first cat's sterilization, but rather "feline influenza."

We immediately took all our cats to another clinic for testing, and the results confirmed it was feline influenza. The vet at the new clinic asked detailed questions about their history. Since the first cat to get sick was the one we had sterilized earlier this month, and the onset of symptoms coincided with the time we were boarding them at this animal hospital, it was concluded that they were likely kept in the same room as the infected cat, thus contracting the disease.

This clinic is very expensive; each visit involves both examination and vet fees. Because we love all our cats, we were always willing to pay. However, we never imagined that our trust in this clinic, simply because of a single sterilization procedure, would result in all 11 adult cats in our home contracting feline influenza, and putting 5 newborn kittens at high risk as well. This has significantly increased our treatment costs.

This experience was terrible for us, and we hope this animal hospital learns from this incident. Don't keep sick cats in the same room with healthy cats, as it will cause owners immense financial and emotional losses later on.
